spells.fillerNotes: 4th slot flexible: God of Battles (team damage buff) or Breaker of Shields (duel burst). Wiki agrees: God of Battles, Warlord's Greeting, and Flying Reaper are near-mandatory; the last slot is a choice of Heat of Battle, Charge, or Breaker of Shields - Heat of Battle is the most popular pick, matching Amya's own choice. - Amya

builds.name: Heavy Armor/Epic Armor
builds.summary: Mostly played around the horse - Right Click into horse turn-and-attack is the primary damage loop, camera-draggable to extend the swing. Once dismounted, Shift-AA into block cancels the animation for repeated hits. Full-commit ground combo: Warlord's Greeting -> Flying Reaper (ult) -> Shift-AA chain. "Learning how to space, what spell can you cancel with heat of battle, and to be pro-active while not losing horse will be key to being useful as glaive!"

builds.name: Medium Armour
builds.summary: Full Strength, medium armor to amplify blunt damage. Relies on Turn-and-Attack + Right-Click horseback damage for sustained pressure, Flying Reaper for burst and control on the ground, and Heat of Battle to cancel enemy spells and survive pressure while dismounted.

not enough personal damage and low mobility to win 1v1s - by design, a bad matchup.

techniques.name: Animation canceling
steps: Training room: try roll-canceling, dismount-canceling and blocking on every skill to learn which are cancelable.
techniques.rhythm: Amya: EVERY CLASS CAN DO IT! - Blocking is the primary cancel; roll canceling interrupts full spells, dismounts, and creates movement otherwise impossible. Costs extra stamina.

techniques.name: Active blocking
steps: it can be BROKEN and stagger you
techniques.rhythm: Don't get "Block checked" - Being an active blocker prevents undesired skills landing on you.

techniques.name: Horse-whistle CC immunity
steps: Time the whistle on the enemy CC
you take damage but no CC
techniques.rhythm: bugs out with PIN/LOCK skills, so care

techniques.name: Walk into braced units
steps: Walk (don't sprint) into their minimal range
techniques.rhythm: brace damage scales with your speed towards them - For braced units like Forte, Halberds, Phalanx - niche: enemy hero outnumbered, unaware or afk.

techniques.name: Turn and Attack
steps: drag camera during the swing to extend its arc
techniques.rhythm: core mounted damage loop, played around constantly - Six patch changes (2025-06-04, verbatim numbered list): more damage vs multiple enemies; better hitbox; -30% damage taken while active; each unit hit reduces its cooldown by 2s (cap 20s); more damage at high horse speed; less stamina cost for Right-Click Attack on horseback.

techniques.name: Shift-AA cancel chain
steps: into block to cancel the animation
immediately Shift-AA again for repeated quick hits
techniques.rhythm: primary dismounted burst tool - Works once dismounted; chains for burst damage.

gameplay.text: Glaive is a mounted-focused hero with high burst and team utility. Due to nerfs to foot-based skills, it rely less on being a burst class on foot. It excels as a mounted brawler and team buffer. You play around Turn & Attack, horse auto-attacks, and once on ground: buffs + burst, then disengage.

However glaive has lackluster dueling abilities and low mobility. Glaive offensive skills can be somewhat tricky to hit on heroes. This can be helped in group fights by using them on enemies who are already stunned by other heroes.

roleLabel: Glaive is a heavy support class, focused on helping allied units and heroes using God of Battles and stunning enemies with Flying Reaper and Warlord's Greeting.

positioning.intro: Where to be during a fight:

bullets.text: Support your own units/heroes - stay close enough that God of Battles' damage buff actually lands on allies, not off alone as a solo skirmisher.
Land your CC as a team follow-up, not a solo opener - Glaive offensive skills can be tricky to hit on heroes, so use them on enemies already stunned by other heroes.
Stay mobile on horseback, commit to a dismounted burst window opportunistically, then re-mount or retreat rather than staying committed on foot.
Watch out for heavily poison-stacked ranged formations - stacked poison debuffs can make a diving Glaive's damage negligible.
no other weapon class in the game has a skill that directly increases allies' damage - it's the class's core team-support tool.

bullets.lead: Warlord's Greeting and Flying Reaper are your CC:
bullets.text: Warlord's Greeting inflicts concussed, which most control-removal skills can't counter; Flying Reaper inflicts thrown and doubles as your own control-effect removal.
Heat of Battle for control removal and defense - the most popular pick; Charge for mobility to retreat or engage; or Breaker of Shields for single-target dueling damage.

bullets.lead: Arc of Steel is the worst skill in the class -
bullets.text: arguably one of the worst weapon skills overall - very low damage, no special effects. Don't build around it.

bullets.lead: Hail of Blades is the weaker paragon:
bullets.text: much less preferred over Flying Reaper due to low impact, weaker control effect, and ease of interruption - Flying Reaper is the default pick.
Learning exactly which enemy skills you can cancel with Heat of Battle, and staying proactive without losing your horse, are the class's core skill-expression points.
Flying Reaper's windup is interruptible by fast-CC classes if thrown out recklessly - don't open with it blind, wait for a window where the target is occupied or your escape/cleanse is up.

bullets.lead: Active blocking stops their CC too:
bullets.text: block helps prevent undesired skills landing on you - Nodachi bloodthirsty CC, Glaive's own Warlord's Greeting CC, Poleaxe's kit (except pin), etc. Watch your block value.
